question: Using a fixed scoring function (train-set item popularity, no model needed) applied to the valid split, what is the bootstrap standard deviation of GAUC, nDCG@5, and their average (primary) under resampling of the eligible valid-split users — i.e. what's the inherent sampling-noise floor of the primary metric on this valid split, and does it exceed the ~0.002-0.007 gaps that have separated every accepted vs. rejected candidate so far?
reflection: The min_count RARE-bucket idea degraded validation primary from 0.6041 to 0.6033, following the same early-peak-then-decay curve every other rejected variant has shown — and the magnitude of the loss (-0.0008) is right in the same 0.002-0.007 noise band that has separated *every* accepted vs. rejected candidate for the last 7 iterations, regardless of mechanism (feature, architecture, loss, debiasing, ensembling). That consistency across totally different mechanisms is itself a clue: before spending another guess, I should check whether that band is actually distinguishable from pure evaluation noise given how few "informative" users the valid split has (per node-10's probe: only ~55% of valid users even have ≥5 rows, and GAUC is only computable at all for users with mixed labels).
